> `obs_count` is **not comparable across runs** — most fetchers report rows merged this run, thirteen fall back to the whole store when nothing was written. To ask how big this source is, count the store. See ledger R326 and the comment in `updater/state.py`.

> A `partial` NEVER sets `last_success_utc` (R231). A source reading `last SUCCESS: NEVER` may be ingesting millions of rows perfectly well and failing one sub-unit. Check `obs_count` and the run history before concluding it is dead.

> **A FUTURE `last_obs_date` IS USUALLY CORRECT, NOT A BUG.** Many publishers ship genuine PROJECTIONS: CSO Ireland's `18_Population_Projections` runs to 2057, Estonia's `rahvastik` to 2085, ABS to 2046/2071, UN WPP to 2101, IMF WEO to 2031. `health.py` already separates the two — `frontier` is the furthest period held INCLUDING projections (display only), `newest_obs` filters to periods <= today and is the recency signal — because 28 of 93 units legitimately reported a future frontier. Do NOT "repair" a future date until you have looked at the series key and the year sequence.
>
> What IS a defect: a SENTINEL (9999-12-31, 2999-12-31) or a COUNTER read as a year (years 1, 2, 3 ... contiguous from 1 — no projection starts at year 1). Tell them apart by the key and the sequence, never by the size of the number. See R320/R322 and `tools/audit_impossible_dates.py`, whose bounds (before 1500, after 2200) are deliberately far outside every real projection horizon.

## 3. How it works

**Why this strategy** (registry `strategy_reason`):

> SURS PxWeb v1 (pxweb.stat.si SiStatData) supports selectable time-dimension values, so per-table since=last_obs delta is feasible; restrict time selection to newer values and merge+overwrite each group file rather than re-pulling all time.

**Adapter contract** (registry `adapter`):

- `vintage_signal`: PxWeb per-table last-modified/'updated' metadata on pxweb.stat.si (or stored watermark) to gate re-query; startPeriod from max stored obs_date.
- `since_param`: PxWeb time-variable value selection (filter:item on time) limited to codes > max stored obs_date; table id .px suffix is stripped when building the series-key prefix.
- `out_paths_note`: per-group parquet files data/clean_full/stat_slovenia/<grp>.parquet (~143 files; group = first 3 chars of the .px table id, e.g. 021, 05G, 071) plus cached _catalog.json — many group files; merge per group.
- `rate_note`: No API key; custom UA; RATE=0.3s; HTTP 429 -> 30s sleep; MAX_CELLS=100000 cap downsamples oversized tables (time full).

**Fetcher module**: [`updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_slovenia.py`](../../updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_slovenia.py)

<details><summary>Its own module docstring — the authoritative description, including every defect previously found and why the code looks the way it does</summary>

```
S3 fetcher — Statistics Slovenia (SURS), PxWeb v1 (pxweb.stat.si SiStatData).

License CC BY 4.0, no API key. Despite the strategy name `sdmx_delta`, SURS exposes
a **PxWeb** API (not SDMX 2.1): per-table JSON metadata listing variables/values, and
a POST query that selects explicit value codes per dimension and returns JSON-stat2.
The S3 contract's "PxWeb branch" applies verbatim: POST the table query with the time
dimension restricted to the codes AFTER the stored max(obs_date).

Layout (set by jobs/ingest_stat_slovenia.py — reused verbatim here):
  ONE parquet per GROUP under clean_full/stat_slovenia/<grp>.parquet, where
  grp = first 3 chars of the .px table id (e.g. 0300220S.px -> "030"). A group file
  holds MANY tables. Schema is the simple 3-column shape:
      series_key : "SI:<table_id_no_px>:<DIM>=<code>:..."   (the .px suffix is stripped)
      obs_date   : date32  (year -> Dec-31, month -> 1st, quarter -> first month, ...)
      value      : float64
  (series_key, obs_date) is the unique key — dedup_keys for the merge.

Each CATALOG TABLE is a sub-unit. For every table we:
  1. read its group parquet to learn THIS table's max(obs_date) and the exact codes it
     already wrote (per-table, by splitting series_key on ':'),
  2. GET the table's PxWeb metadata (variables + value lists),
  3. resolve THE time dimension with the shared value-first resolver (core/pxweb.py:
     authoritative `time: true` code, else highest date-parse-rate, else literal name —
     the SAME axis _parse_jsonstat2 keys obs_date on), parse every time code to a date,
     and keep ONLY codes whose date > stored max  (date-tail: tiny query),
  4. replicate the ingester's dimension selection — the all-values-vs-one-aggregate branch
     is decided on the FULL total_cells (NOT the date-restricted count) so the series_keys
     produced match the ones already on disk EXACTLY (no parallel keys); ONLY the resolved
     time axis is restricted to the new codes (the OLD builder restricted EVERY time-ish
     variable, so a month+year cube had BOTH axes filtered to "newer" period codes — the
     month selection was emptied of valid codes and the tail silently froze),
  5. POST the query, parse JSON-stat2 with the SAME parser as the ingester, accumulate the
     rows under the table's group,
  6. merge each touched group file via merge.merge_and_write(..., mode="merge",
     dedup_keys=("series_key","obs_date")) — never write parquet directly, never shrink.

Honest status (Tally + finalize):
  - timeout / 5xx / 429 / network drop / bad-json after retries  -> transient_unit() -> run is 'partial'
  - 200 metadata whose `variables` block is gone/empty, OR a 200 POST that parsed 0 rows
    from a NON-trivial body on a FULL (no date restriction) fetch of a populated table
                                                                  -> structural_unit() -> DefinitiveError
  - first-seen NEW table (no on-disk history) that yields rows    -> added_unit(n)
  - table already current (no time codes newer than max), or a legitimately-quiet tail
                                                                  -> empty_unit()
empty_window_floor = (#sub-units) - 1, so only a TRULY total all-empty window trips the
wholesale-outage floor — a healthy monthly run where most of 4,696 tables have nothing new
is legitimate no_change, caught precisely per-table via structural_unit().
```

</details>

## 4. If it stops updating — diagnose in this order

Run everything from `E:\research\econfindatalibrary`.

```bash
# 1. What does the system actually say? (not what you remember)
python -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config;con=sqlite3.connect(f'file:{config.STATE_DB}?mode=ro',uri=True);print(*con.execute(\"SELECT unit_id,status,last_success_utc,last_attempt_utc,last_error FROM unit_state WHERE source_id='stat_slovenia'\"),sep=chr(10))"

# 2. Is it even being ATTEMPTED? 'scheduled' is not 'attempted' (R246).
#    A daily run reaches ~20 of ~106 cloud sources; most are skipped on cadence, which is normal.
python -m updater.run --source stat_slovenia --dry

# 3. Run it for real and READ THE REASON. Failures name themselves now.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -u -m updater.run --source stat_slovenia --force

# 4. Is the PUBLISHER healthy, or is it us? Probe upstream directly, never a relay.
#    (DBnomics is BANNED — every source must be reached at its own publisher.)

# 5. Is the store intact? obs_count in state is NOT the answer.
AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2 python -c "import sys,os;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from updater import config,blob;d=config.source_dir('stat_slovenia');fs=[f for f in blob.list_parquets(d) if not os.path.basename(f).startswith('_')];print(len(fs),'files',sum(blob.row_count(os.path.join(d,os.path.basename(f))) for f in fs),'rows')"

# 6. Are its dates real? A counter-as-year or a 9999 sentinel is silent (7 sources hit).
#    NOTE: a FUTURE date is usually a legitimate projection - check the key before repairing.
python tools/audit_impossible_dates.py --r2 --source stat_slovenia
```

**Read the failure class before fixing anything.** From the 2026-08-04 audit of every unfetchable source, the causes were: `budget_deferral` (NOT broken — ran out of its time slice), `code_bug`, `rate_limited`, `gated_by_design`. **Zero** were an expired credential or a dead endpoint, although that is the usual first guess.

If the error names sub-units as `deferred (budget N min)` or `budget spent`, **nothing has failed** — the source ran out of its slice and the rest is taken next tick (R303). Do not 'fix' it.

## 4b. Root cause when this was last investigated (2026-08-04)

*From the unfetchable-source audit — 29 agents, every finding challenged by a skeptic before it was accepted. This source was covered by the target `stat_slovenia`.*

- **root cause**: `code_bug`  (confidence high)
- **which units**: 1 of 85 attempted sub-units in the 2026-08-04 slice: table 2221405S.px (group 222, "Public scheduled road passenger transport (interurban and international) by MEASURES, INTERURBAN/INTERNATIONAL TRANSPORT, DISTANCE and YEAR"). The fetcher never labels its structural_unit() calls, so the id had to be recovered by re-running the fetcher's own code read-only. NOTE: the brief's premise is WRONG — there is no shape mismatch. The response shape is exactly what the parser expects; SURS published an empty (all-null) 2024 year slot on a table last updated 2018-10-19, and our inline gate misreads a 36-element all-null array as a "non-trivial body".
- **blast radius**: Zero rows lost — merge is untouched and 249.parquet grew 501,866 -> 876,614 rows during the same run. But the ONE sub-unit sinks the ENTIRE source: finalize() raises DefinitiveError, update() never returns a Result, and orchestrate.py:937-939 records 'partial' while discarding last_obs_date, obs_count, series_cursors and last_success_utc. Measured in data/_aqueduct/state.db: unit_state(stat_slovenia,_all) has last_success_utc=None, last_obs_date=None, obs_count=None, and there is NO source_state row at all. Every recorded run since 2026-07-14 ended this way (2/442, 4/510, 3/3, 1/85), so the source has never gone green and, because series_cursors is dropped, _derive_changed_csvs has never run for it — published CSVs never follow the parquet. Scale: 4,696 tables / 145 groups / 150 group parquet files. Same defect class present in 2 sibling fetchers (hagstofa.py:382, statfin.py:590); hagstofa's run 9 minutes later on 2026-08-04 produced the identical error shape (2/1074, offenders UMH11120.px and UMH11165.px).
- fixable by us: **True**

**Recommended fix, in order:**

> Two-line change in updater/strategies/fetchers/stat_slovenia.py. (1) At lines 735-737 replace the inline gate with the shared rule already used by bfs and stat_estonia: `from ._common import structural_on_zero_rows` and `if structural_on_zero_rows(safe_max, resp): tally.structural_unit(tid) else: current += 1`. Use `safe_max` (computed at line 682), not the raw `stored_max`, which is what that helper's contract requires. This makes an all-null value array — a period slot SURS published ahead of its data — a confirmed-quiet sub-unit instead of a fabricated schema break, and 2221405S.px stops sinking the source. (2) Pass a label to every tally.structural_unit()/transient_unit() call (lines 623, 634, 662, 737) so the error message names the offending table id; _common._named already renders up to 20 of them and orchestrate._clip_err now carries 1400 chars. Without this the finding costs a 40-minute bisect, which is exactly why it has sat unfixed since 2026-07-14. Then apply the same fix to the two siblings in the class: hagstofa.py:382 and statfin.py:590. Nothing here is a data repair — no rows were ever lost; the fix is purely to stop a valid empty response from being reported as a structural break and blocking last_success_utc, the vintage bump and the CSV re-derive for all 4,696 tables. Separately (lower priority, spotted in passing, not the cause): stat_slovenia strips '.px' case-sensitively at lines 619/606, so catalog ids ending '.PX' keep the suffix in their series_key and cursors (e.g. '2490109S.PX'), and the fetcher never calls Tally.deferred_unit(), so its 40-minute budget stop is invisible to finalize() and cannot be reported as an R303 deferral.

## 6. Rules that apply to every repair here

- **A key/parser change is a RE-PULL, never a merge** (R22). Changing what `series_key` means leaves the old and new grains coexisting; dedup cannot collapse them because they no longer collide. Use `mode="replace"`, or re-pull the table.
- **Never patch dates — re-pull** (R288). A naive date repair on `cso` would have destroyed 11 of 12 rows; only a negative control caught it. And 41,091 of `stat_slovenia`'s fabricated dates land in 1900–2200, indistinguishable from real data, so no date test can find them.
- **Verify against the store you are actually serving** (R296/R36). Under `AQUEDUCT_BACKEND=r2` the local directory is a scratch mirror of the last run only; a local check can under-report or give the opposite answer.
- **When a probe reports ABSENCE, run it against something known PRESENT** (R316). An absence looks identical whether the data is missing or the probe is broken.
- **Compare (key, date) pairs, not just keys** (R314). A re-key check that compares identifiers verifies the half you changed on purpose; the half you changed by accident is in the values.
- **A bound over a fixed order is a truncation, not a budget** (R190). If work is capped, check it ROTATES — and specifically that it rotates when the item at the head never completes (R313).
- **Read the job's ARGV, not its progress** (R323). A `--dry-run` and a real run print the same numbers.
